existing.description: The Institut Pasteur runs the Pasteur-Paris University (PPU) international doctoral programme with Université Paris Cité, Sorbonne Université and Université Paris Saclay for candidates holding a Master's degree or equivalent in life or medical sciences. Selected students are employees of the Institut Pasteur on a three-year working contract and receive a monthly salary of EUR 2,000 inclusive of social benefits, a EUR 4,000 welcome bonus, annual round-trip travel reimbursement and EUR 750 per year for conferences or summer courses. The 2027 call for enrolment in October 2027 is open from 1 October to 16 November 2026, with around 15 places offered each year through a three-stage selection ending in an interview week at Institut Pasteur in February 2027.
eligibility: Master's degree or an equivalent university degree in science, medicine or related fields from a university located outside France, by the time the programme begins
Students holding a B.A. or B.S. acquired after four years of academic education may be considered with at least 6 months of laboratory experience and a written final report or publication
Students who have already begun doctoral training elsewhere, and students with a Master's degree obtained in France, are not eligible for PPU-Classic, PPU-OXFORD, PPU-EID and PPU-Imagine
Students should not have resided in France for more than 12 months in the three years immediately prior to the application deadline
Candidates must be selected by a host laboratory as part of the application
Host thesis advisors must hold an HDR diploma and the host laboratory must be affiliated with Institut Pasteur Paris and a doctoral school of a partner university
existing.eligibility_summary: Master's degree or equivalent university degree in science, medicine or related fields delivered by a university outside France, obtainable by the start of the programme. Holders of a B.A. or B.S. after four years may be considered with at least six months of laboratory experience evidenced by a written final report or publication. Candidates must not have resided in France for more than 12 months in the three years before the deadline. No age restriction and no nationality restriction.
benefits: Three-year working contract as an Institut Pasteur employee
Monthly salary of EUR 2,000 including social benefits
EUR 4,000 gross welcome bonus paid with the first salary
Annual round-trip travel reimbursement for the country of origin
EUR 750 per year for conferences or summer courses
Assistance finding accommodation in student residences, including the Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris
One-to-one meetings with the Dean of the PPU and administrative support from the Doctoral Student Office
Subsidised cafeteria lunches, campus conferences and reduced-fee access to Institut Pasteur and university amenities
Free access to the Centre for Scientific Information
coverage: Monthly salary of EUR 2,000 comprehensive of social benefits (national health care, health insurance)
One-off welcome bonus of EUR 4,000 gross
Reimbursement of one round-trip ticket per year (train or plane, eco-class): up to EUR 1,300 for non-continental European countries and up to EUR 350 for continental European countries
EUR 750 per year per student for international conferences or summer courses
Assistance with accommodation in the first year
Access to Institut Pasteur and university amenities at reduced fees, subsidised cafeteria lunches and free WiFi
Free access to the Centre for Scientific Information
requirements: Create an account on the PPU platform at https://ppu.pasteur.fr to view projects and apply
Select up to four host-laboratory projects during the call
Upload a detailed CV and a motivation letter in PDF format
Complete the joint application with the host laboratory in November, choosing one single project and programme
No application by email is accepted
Candidates who apply to several laboratories may apply to a maximum of four
documents: Detailed CV in PDF format uploaded on the PPU platform
Motivation letter in PDF format uploaded on the PPU platform
Copy of the Master's diploma or a certified written attestation of completion, available before the start of the programme
existing.english_requirement: The programme is run in English and fluency in English is required. TOEFL or other language proficiency scores are not necessary but may be indicated. No knowledge of French is required.
application_method: Register on the PPU application platform and choose up to four research projects
Upload a detailed CV and motivation letter in PDF format through the platform
Have the selected host laboratory submit the joint application on the same platform
Present past and future work at an interview week at Institut Pasteur
existing.selection_notes: Three-stage selection: host-laboratory selection, evaluation of joint applications by the Admission Committee in December on academic qualifications, previous research experience, scientific potential and fit to the proposed project, then a four-day interview week at Institut Pasteur. Around 15 openings are available each year and admission is highly competitive.
existing.best_fit: Life-science and medical-science Master's graduates (or final-year students) from outside France who can be selected by a host laboratory at Institut Pasteur and do not meet the 12-month France residency limit.
existing.application_period: Host-laboratory applications open 1 October 2026 and close 16 November 2026; shortlisted candidates submit the joint application by 14 December 2026; interviews take place at Institut Pasteur in early March 2027 with decisions shortly after.
existing.deadline_display: The call for enrollment of students in October 2027 will be open from October 1st to November 16th, 2026

scholarships.title: InLife International Mobility Grants 2026-2027
scholarships.official_source: InLife - Initiative Sciences aux interfaces du vivant (Sorbonne Université)

existing.description: InLife, the Initiative Sciences aux interfaces du vivant of Sorbonne Université, awards three incoming mobility grants of EUR 7,500 for 2026-2027 to Master's students coming from foreign universities to laboratories affiliated with Sorbonne University Alliance. The grant covers travel and accommodation expenses, and the intern also receives the standard stipend for a Master 2 internship; additional stipend funding may be requested from InLife in the project description. The host laboratory must be affiliated with a Sorbonne University Alliance institution and projects must be interdisciplinary at the interface of fields related to the study of living systems. Applications are submitted as a single PDF by email and are evaluated by the members of the InLife Executive Committee.
eligibility: Master's (Master 2) student from a foreign university
Hosting laboratory must be affiliated with an institution within the Sorbonne University Alliance
Project must be interdisciplinary at the interface of fields related to the study of living systems
No geographical restriction on the university of origin
existing.eligibility_summary: Master's students from foreign universities, hosted by a laboratory affiliated with an institution within Sorbonne University Alliance, on interdisciplinary projects at the interface of fields related to the study of living systems. There are no geographical restrictions regarding the university of origin.
benefits: EUR 7,500 mobility grant covering travel and accommodation
Standard stipend for a Master 2 internship
Possibility of additional InLife stipend funding if requested in the project description
coverage: Standard stipend for a Master 2 internship paid by the host arrangement
Possible additional InLife stipend funding if requested in the project description
requirements: Project description must be one page and contain 5 key words
Description of the context, questions and approaches
Explain the interdisciplinary dimension of the project
State whether the project is part of an active or new collaboration with a foreign laboratory
documents: CV of the project leader (1 page)
CV and grades of the candidate, with rankings if possible (1 page)
Project description (1 page) including 5 key words
application_method: Send a single PDF by email to initiative-inlife@sorbonne-universite.fr
Include the project leader's CV, the candidate's CV and grades, and a one-page project description
existing.best_fit: Master 2 students from foreign universities seeking a research placement in a Sorbonne University Alliance laboratory on an interdisciplinary life-sciences interface project.
existing.application_period: Single annual call for 2026-2027, published 6 July 2026 and updated 29 September 2026, closing 2 November 2026 at 18:00.
existing.deadline_display: Deadline for application: November 2, 2026 at 6 pm
